label: Pocket money
blurb: Your parents give you money each month — sometimes late. No bank account yet; you use the family phone for UPI.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. Pocket money arrives when it arrives.
stageIntro.2: Five years later: your first job. Your parents still ask what you're saving.
stageIntro.3: Six more years: a raise, a family of your own, and bigger decisions.

label: Scholarship
blurb: Your ePASS allowance lands in your own bank account as a lump sum, plus a little from family. You share a phone.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. The allowance just landed — all of it at once.
stageIntro.2: Five years later: first salary, your own phone, and relatives with expectations.
stageIntro.3: Six more years: a raise, EMIs on offer everywhere, and a goal that matters.

label: Earner
blurb: You work evenings at a shop. Pay is weekly and uneven, and part of it goes home. Own phone, own UPI.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. Shifts after college, cash on Sundays.
stageIntro.2: Five years later: a steady salary for the first time. Home still counts on you.
stageIntro.3: Six more years: a raise, and the question of what all this work was for.
